limitations_and_boundaries: The main blocker for future work (and biggest limitation of our work) is the lack of a public, highly curated, and large benchmark for causal discovery. Scalability experiments were limited to inference on synthetic data.
The approach assumes nonlinear additive Gaussian noise models; it fails to identify the causal graph under linear functions.
For d=500 and SCORE method, experiments could not be repeated in a reasonable time; values refer to a single run.

research_questions.statement: Can the full causal DAG be recovered from the second derivative of the log-likelihood (score function) in observational nonlinear additive Gaussian noise models?

provenance.text_excerpt: Theoretically, this implies that we can get rid of the costly pruning step in SCORE (Rolland et al. (2022)) as all information about the causal structure is already contained in the Jacobian of the score.

claims.statement: All information about the causal structure is already contained in the Jacobian of the score, eliminating the need for the costly pruning step in SCORE.

provenance.text_excerpt: In this work, we show that the second derivative of the log-likelihood allows to recover both the skeleton and the direction of the edges in the causal DAG.

claims.statement: The second derivative of the log-likelihood allows recovery of both the skeleton and the direction of edges in the causal DAG.

experiments_or_tasks: Demonstrate theoretically that the second derivative of the log-likelihood allows recovery of both skeleton and direction of edges in the causal DAG, extending prior work that only recovered topological order.

methods.name: Score-based causal discovery theory
methods.protocol_description: Under the assumption of nonlinear additive Gaussian noise models, analyze the Jacobian of the score function to show that it contains all information about the causal structure, enabling recovery of the full DAG without the costly pruning step required by SCORE.

study_units.name: Theoretical analysis of score-based causal discovery

research_questions.statement: How does the proposed DAS algorithm compare to state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and scalability?

provenance.text_excerpt: DAS ... reduces the complexity of the pruning by a factor proportional to the graph size.

claims.statement: DAS reduces the complexity of the pruning step by a factor proportional to the graph size.

provenance.text_excerpt: DAS achieves competitive accuracy with current state-of-the-art while being over an order of magnitude faster.

claims.statement: DAS achieves competitive accuracy with current state-of-the-art while being over an order of magnitude faster.

provenance.text_excerpt: we designed an algorithm that is more efficient by a factor of O(d) compared to Rolland et al. (2022)

claims.statement: DAS is more efficient by a factor of O(d) compared to SCORE.

datasets.description: Synthetic data generated from Erdos-Renyi graphs with expected degree 4 (ER4) under nonlinear additive Gaussian noise models.
datasets.name: ER4 synthetic data

experiments_or_tasks: Compare DAS against SCORE, CAM, and GraNDAG on synthetic data generated from ER4 graphs with varying number of nodes (d=10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000).
Measure structural Hamming distance (SHD), structural intervention distance (SID), precision, recall, and execution time.

methods.name: DAS (Discovery At Scale)
methods.protocol_description: DAS first estimates the score function to recover topological order, then uses the Jacobian of the score to select candidate edges via a t-test with p-value ≤0.01, and finally applies CAM-pruning to reduce false positives. Complexity is O(dn^3 + d^2).

methods.name: SCORE
methods.protocol_description: SCORE estimates the score function, recovers topological order from the Jacobian, and prunes using CAM. Bottleneck is the pruning step with complexity O(d * t * r(n,d)).

methods.name: CAM
methods.protocol_description: CAM uses a greedy search with generalized additive models and pruning. Results taken from Rolland et al. (2022).

methods.name: GraNDAG
methods.protocol_description: GraNDAG uses a continuous optimization approach with a DAG constraint. Results taken from Rolland et al. (2022).

study_units.name: Empirical evaluation of DAS on synthetic data
